original_question: Suppose S3 → S7 → S4 is a “generalized” Hopf fibration. Does there exist a homology 4-sphere H and a degree one map H → S4 such that the pull-back of the generalized Hopf fibration is a flat S3 -bundle?
target_in_paper: Question 3.12 (Freedman) in §3.4, "Milnor-Wood inequality, Euler class and Godbillon-Vey class".
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation. It has the correct bundle diagram S^3 -> S^7 -> S^4, keeps the paper’s quoted phrase "generalized" Hopf fibration, asks for a homology 4-sphere H, asks for a degree-one map H -> S^4, and asks whether the pullback becomes a flat S^3-bundle. That is exactly the content of Question 3.12.
missing_details: The exact target is Question 3.12 (Freedman) in §3.4; the paper places it specifically in the discussion of higher-dimensional Milnor-Wood phenomena and controlled Mather-Thurston theory.
To make "degree one" fully well-posed, H should be understood as a closed oriented homology 4-sphere, and the map H -> S^4 should have orientation degree 1.
The nearby paragraph indicates that "flat" is meant in the topological/C^0 sense: Mather-Thurston theory for C^0-foliations produces a flat C^0 S^3-bundle.

The paper does not locally define the phrase "generalized" Hopf fibration any further, so a faithful standalone rewrite should retain that phrase rather than replace it with a stronger external definition.
There is no explicit equivalent reformulation proved nearby; the remarks about bordism and semi-s-cobordism are motivation, not a stated equivalence.
refined_question: Question 3.12 (Freedman). Suppose S^3 -> S^7 -> S^4 is a "generalized" Hopf fibration. Does there exist a closed oriented homology 4-sphere H and a degree-one map f: H -> S^4 such that the pullback of this S^3-bundle along f is a flat S^3-bundle over H (in the topological/C^0 sense used in the surrounding discussion)?
justification: The draft matches Question 3.12 essentially verbatim, so this is clearly the intended target rather than any neighboring problem. The surrounding discussion on pp. 11-12 shows why the question is being asked: Theorem 3.10 records unbounded Euler and first Pontryagin classes for S^3-bundles, the paragraph immediately before Question 3.12 singles out flat S^3-bundles as especially interesting because of Freedman’s controlled Mather-Thurston perspective, and the paragraph immediately after Question 3.12 clarifies that Mather-Thurston gives bordism to a flat C^0 S^3-bundle and motivates a semi-s-cobordism viewpoint. Because the paper itself leaves "generalized Hopf fibration" informal, the sharpest faithful rewrite is to preserve that exact phrase and only make explicit the orientation/closedness needed for the degree-one map.
